texts.preamble: M/S Nonand Rai Bhola Nath vs M/S Shri Krishna Masala Co on 9 December, 2024 In The Court Of Sh. Mukesh Kumar Gupta, District Judge (Commercial Court)-07, Central District. Tis Hazari Courts, New Delhi. Cs (Comm) No. 1127/2024 M/s Nonand Rai Bhola Nath Versus M/s Shri Krishna Masala Co. Date on which order was reserved : 27.11.2024
texts.facts: Eschewing prolix reference to the pleadings, crystallizing the same, the case of the plaintiff as averred in the plaint is that: MUKESH by KUMAR GUPTA 2.1) Plaintiff company is manufacturing, marketing and selling of KUMAR Date: GUPTA Chatni, spices, fruit flavouring, edible flavouring essence & food colors, 2024.12.09 17:58:42 -0800 sauces, condiments, dry fruits, thandai power, instant powder drinks, preserved, dried cooked, tinned, canned fruits, foods and vegetables, kirana products etc. for the past several years with trade mark and copy right NAU BAHAR/ alongwith specified logo or as shown in para no.6 of the plaint and hence the plaintiff is its true and lawful proprietor. The said trademark NAU BAHAR/ has been in continuous and extensive use since the year 1929. 2.2) Plaintiff firm has over decades established a dynamic reputation for itself, by virtue of high quality products which are sold in unique and eye catching packagings which further enhance their appears to the public. As per plaintiff, its products are not only popular in the market but are of excellent international standard and safety and plaintiff has earned good reputation in the market as plaintiff invested its time and resources in undertaking extensive research and development and creating innovative products. The plaintiff has also taken pains to popularize the said trademark among the public by incurring and investing sufficient amount of money, time, energy, skill, effort, labour etc. for the same and thus, it has acquired distinctiveness and recognized well known identity. 2.4) The plaintiff has carried out extensive sales of goods under the said trademarks and packaging labels and established a good business thereunder and the details of yearwise sales of the plaintiff are provided in the below Year Turnover for the Year 2010 - 2011 1,32,00,000.00 (approx.) 2011 - 2012 1,54,00,000.00 (approx.) 2012 - 2013 1,89,00,000.00 (approx.) 2013 - 2014 2,34,00,000.00 (approx.) 2014 - 2015 3,08,00,000.00 (approx.) 2015 - 2016 3,27,00,000.00 (approx.) for identical goods and by adoption and use of the impugned trademark by the defendants amounts to infrigement of registered trademarks "NAU BAHAR/ of the plaintiff and it also results or is liable to or is likely to result in passing off the defendant's products as those of the plaintiff or associated with the plaintiff in one or the other manner. The adoption of the said trademark NAV BAHAR CHATNI by the defendants is wilful, deliberate, dishonest and malafide and is with complete knowlede of the plaintiff's prior registered and well known trademarks "NAU BAHAR/ " and ought to be restrained forthwith. The clear intention of he defendant is to somehow convey to the customer that defendant's product is same, identical, somehow connected with the plaintiff. The use of the said trademark by the defendant is illegal, unauthorized and unjustified. 2.7) It is further the case of the plaintiff that on 06.06.2024, on Digitally coming across the product under the trademark NAV BAHAR CHATNI signed by MUKESH MUKESH of the defendant, plaintiff immediately caused a search into the records of KUMAR KUMAR GUPTA GUPTA Date: 2024.12.09 18:00:57 -0800 Registrar of Trade Marks but no records was found and thereafter, the plaintiff came to know about illegal dishonest and malicious adoption of the said trademark "NAV BAHAR CHATNI" by the defendant. Accordingly, plaintiff issued a cease and desist notice to the defendant through its attorney dated 13.06.2024, thereby calling upon the siad defendant to cease and desist from advertising the impugned trademark and further desist from using the impugned trademark NAV BAHAR CHATNI in future and the defendant replied the same vide reply dated 22.06.2024 by giving evasive replies stating that trademark used by the defendant is the tagline associated with the defendant and there is no likelihood of confusion by use of the said trademark NAV BAHAR CHATNI and the defendant has refused to cease and desist from using the impugned trademark 'NAV BAHAR CHATNI' for goods associated with plaintiff like Chatni spices, fruit flavouring, edible flavouring, essence & food colours, sauces codiments, kirana products and other allied and cognate goods. 2.8) It is further the case of the plaintiff that the defendant has recently adopted identical/deceptively similar trademark for the goods namely the Chatni, spices, fruit flavourings, edible flavouring, essence & food colors, sauces, condiments, Kirana products and other cognate and allied products Thus, the defendant has adopted and used the impugned MUKESH by trademark NAV BAHAR/ NAV BAHAR CHATNI are of the same KUMAR GUPTA KUMAR Date: GUPTA 2024.12.09 18:01:03 -0800 description as those of the goods of the plaintiff which is shown below. PLAINTIFF'S PACKAGING DEFENDANT'S PACKAGING MUKESH by MUKESH KUMAR GUPTA KUMAR 4 GUPTA 2024.12.09 18:01:11 -0800 It has been stated that the Defendant is neither the proprietor nor the permitted user of the said Registered Trademark NAU BAHAR/ and the identical Trademark NAV BAHAR is being used by the Defendant without the leave and license of the Plaintiff and the Defendant has adopted and started using the Trademark NAV BAHAR dishonestly, fraudulently and out of greed with a view to take advantage and to trade upon the established goodwill, reputation and proprietary rights of the Plaintiff. 2.9). It is further the case of the plaintiff that the cause of action arose in favour of the plaintiff for the first time in the first week of June 2024 when paintiff came across the Defendant's product under impugned product 'NAV BAHAR CHATNI' available in the markets of Delhi/NCR. The cause of action further arose on 13.06.2024, when the Plaintiff issued a cease-and-desist notice and refused to desist from infringing activities vide its reply dated 22.06.2024. The cause of action is continuous one and will continue to accrue so long as the defendant is not restrained from using the impugned trade mark/label/name 'NAV BAHAR CHATNI' Hence the present suit. 3. Alongwith the suit, the plaintiff has filed the instant application under Order XXXIX Rule 1 & 2 CPC for grant of restraint order as Digitally signed mentioned above. MUKESH by MUKESH KUMAR GUPTA KUMAR Date: On receipt of summons for settlement of issues, the defendant contested the suit by filing a detailed Written Statement and reply to the interim application thereby taking various preliminary objections as averred and mentioned herein under:- 4.1.) Defendant firm is a partnership firm and is engaged in the business of manufacturing and selling spices, sauces, Kirana products under the brand name of "Shri Krishna". Defendant firm established its business many decades ago by continuous hard work, honestly and purity and enjoying fruits thereof and it promoting its business by way of advertising, contacting its dealers, retailers, sales promotion, research and development by engaging distinct goodwill amongst his customer/consumers and "Shri Krishna" is the original the creation of defendant firm which is having all the trappings of an invented trademark and the same is highly unlikely to portray any deceptive connotations to any existing mark to the ordinary prudent purchaser. 4.2) It has been contended that neither the trade and whole business nor the Trademark of plaintiff company and defendant Firm are similar with each other and does not adversely affect the business of each other and no confusion or deception would be caused to the customers of both the parties in respect of their products so the notice under reply is totally based upon false, fabricated and arm twisting and is M/S Nonand Rai Bhola Nath vs M/S Shri Krishna Masala Co on 9 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65621595/ 5 also misuse of the process of law. The defendant firm has not used as Nau Bahar, the Digitally alleged trademark of the plaintiff and the defendant has never intended signed by MUKESH to use another word "Nav Bahar Chatni" " " "NAU MUKESH KUMAR KUMAR GUPTA GUPTA Date: 2024.12.09 18:01:33 -0800 BAHAR/ and for description of the character or quality of its goods or services that is why the defendant firm till date has not applied for registration of the trademark "Nav Bahar Chatni" " ". He was using bonafide said name or tagline of anyone. 4.3) On merits, the defendant has denied all the allegations of the plaintiff and contended that as per the document filed by the plaintiff, the trademark of the plaintiff is "NAU BAHAR/ and , and Not "Nav Bahar Chatni" " " as has been used by the defendant and thus the plaintiff is not entitled to any relief. The defendant trademark "Nav Bahar Chatni" " " is in a different colur scheme, letters and design from the plaitniff's alleged trademark. 4.4) The defendant has reiterated that its tradmark Shri Krishna adopted in 1965 has its own distinctive goodwill and reputation and the defendant did not ride upon the alleged goodwill or reputation of the plaintiff. It has been claimed that even otherwise a similar trademark can be used by anyone for a substantial different product and no such trademark co-exist in the field of trade. 4.5) The defendant has stated that it has never used nor intended MUKESH by to use the plaintiff's trademark dishonestly and with knowledge as KUMAR GUPTA Date: GUPTA 2024.12.09 18:01:41 -0800 claimed and it has been used only in a descriptive manner nor as a trademark, which the defendant has even discontinued and restrained itself from the use of the word Nav Bahar in their business after receipt of the legal notice from the plaintiff's firm. The defendant has claimed dismissal of the suit as also the interim application. 5. In reply to the application u/o XXXIX Rule 1 and 2 CPC, the defendant has denied the contents of the application and reiterated the contents of the Written Statement seeking a dismissal of the interim application with exemplary costs.
texts.arguments: Finally, it has been contended that there is absolutely no cause of action in favour of plaintiff and against the defendant and the suit filed by the plaintiff is nothing and an attempt to armstwist the defendant with an open threat that the plaintiff may implicate the defendant into false cases. 6 7. At the outset, in order to obtain an ad-interim injunction u/o XXXIX Rule 1 and 2 CPC the plaintiff has to satisfy the court on the trinity principle of strong prima facie case, balance of convenience and irreparable loss and injury which cannot be monetarily compensated. 8. The crux of the legal precedents can be seen from the celebrated Gujrat Bottling Co. Ltd. Vs. Coca Cola Company & Ors. [(1996) (16) PTC 89 (SC)], which is the landmark judgment and holds the legal field till date. The Hon'ble Apex Court has observed: ".....The object of the interlocutory injunction is to protect the plaintiff against injury by violation of his right for which he could not be adequately compensated in damages recoverable in the action if the uncertainty were resolved in his favour at the trial. The need for such protection has, however, to be weighed against the corresponding need of the defendant to be protected against injury resulting from his having been prevented from exercising his own legal rights for which he could not be adequately compensated. The court must weigh need against another and determine where the "balance of convenience" lies' "Prima facie case" means that the Court should be satisfied that there is a serious question to be tried at the hearing, and there is a probability of plaintiff obtaining the relief at the conclusion of the trial on the basis of the material placed before the Court. In case tiled as Mumtaz Ahmed Vs Pakeeza Chemicals, AIR 2003 AII 114, where it has been held that, "in order to come to the conclusion whether one mark is deceptively similar to another, the broad and essential features of the two are to be considered. They should not be placed side by side, to find out if there are any differences, in the design, and if, so whether they are of such a character as to prevent one design from being mistaken for the other. 11. In case titled as BDH Industries Ltd Vs. Croydon Chemical Works Pvt Ltd., AIR 2002 Bom. 361, where in it has been held that, "apart from the structural, visual and phonetic similarity or dissimilarity, the question has to be considered from the point of view of man of average intelligence and imperfect collection. by MUKESH MUKESH KUMAR KUMAR GUPTA Date: GUPTA 2024.12.09 18:02:02 -0800 12 Hon'ble Supreme Court while explaining the phrase li deceive or cause confusion, relying upon the judgment of privy council in Pianotist Co. Application (1906) 23 RPC 774 has held that: "For deceptive resemblance two important questions are: (1) who are the persons whom the resemblance must be likely to deceive or confuse and (2) what rules of comparison are to be adopted in judging whether such resemblance exists. As to confusion, it is perhaps an appropriate description of the state of mind of a customer who, on seeing a mark thinks that it differs from the mark on goods which he has previously bought, but is doubtful whether that impression is not due to imperfect recollection". 12. Dealing with passing off, in the matter of Laxmikant Vs. Patel AIR 2002 SC 295, the Hon'ble Supreme Court has observed that it is common in the trade and business to adopt a name, and the courts should protect the goodwill attached to the business name. An action of passing off will lie wherever the intended name is calculated to deceive or to divert the business from the plaintiff or to cause confusion between the two business. For deceptive resemblance, the two important questions are who are the persons whom the resemblance must be likely to deceive or confuse, and what rules of comparison are to be adopted, in judging, whether such resemblance exists. The user of the MUKESH by MUKESH plaintiff's trademark "NAU BAHAR/ by the defendant is KUMAR KUMAR GUPTA Date: GUPTA 2024.12.09 18:02:22 -0800 sufficient to create a reasonable doubt in the minds of consumers regarding the origin of the products and resultant loss of the business and reputation of the plaintiff's company.
